$comment: Gemfall beat 5 on the River Road (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 5A). `allies` is set exactly once, by the three choices of scene_who_to_tell, which every path to every ending passes through once (it sits before the crossing and nothing loops back). `cult` is optional and only ever set by scene_cult_pitch, on one of two choices, so no path sets both. The setback needs a failed span crossing, then a failed wolf check or the fight picked, and the fight lost. The expansion's spine episodes (brass south, tremor, Nim's pony, old marks, survey guard, crack string, stones vote, span question, pack crossing, rim lookout) set only chapter-local flags; allies is still set only in scene_who_to_tell.
title: The Broken Bridge

objectives.label: Helped somebody whose rush was over
Plotted the outline of the truth yourselves

facet_clerks.name: The Clerk's Stone
facet_clerks.text: Logged, tagged 4117, and crossing westbound. Then, very irregularly, not.

scene_bridge.narration: The Northern River Bridge has a crack down the middle like a dropped plate glued back by somebody in a hurry. Skywardens in silver and violet stand on every span with chalk and clipboards, letting people over a few at a time. Coming the other way, south, is everybody whose rush is already over, and none of them are singing.

scene_spans_from_above.narration: From the air the crack is not one crack. It is dozens, and they all lean the same way, like grass in a wind. The wind is coming from the mountain. A warden engineer on the bridge looks up, sees you, and writes something down.

scene_soup_line.narration: Further along the line is a pot of soup the size of a bathtub. The woman stirring it hands a bowl to a muddy prospector before she says a single word to anyone. Her name is Hollis. Her apron says DEEP HOLLOW in small, tidy stitches. Behind her, the prospector's wheelbarrow has lost a wheel.

choices.label: Thank her and keep your place

scene_soup_line_fix_barrow.narration: You find the wheel in the ditch and knock it back on with a rock. The prospector watches you do it with his soup bowl in both hands, and when it is done he digs in his pocket and gives you the only thing he has left: a pebble he carried the whole way north for luck. It is not a gem. He says it worked anyway.

scene_cult_pitch.narration: Hollis talks while she ladles, gently, like she's telling you the weather. "The world's rules are broken, love. Look at this line. The power under the mountain could write new ones. The seal on it isn't a lock. It's a lid on the cure." She nods at a jar labeled THE BREAK. It is half full of humming stones.

choices.label: Drop a coin in the jar
Finish your soup and say nothing

scene_cult_pitch_finish_soup.narration: You finish your soup and say nothing. Hollis refills the bowl without asking, and says nothing either, and watches you go with the ladle resting on her shoulder. The jar hums behind her. You can still hear it at the bridge foot.

choices.label: Walk on to the bridge foot

scene_cult_pitch_drop_stone.narration: You drop a coin into the jar marked THE BREAK, in among the humming stones. The whole jar hums louder for a moment, like a hive woken up. Hollis's eyes shine. She writes your names in a little book with a soft pencil, and gives each of you a second bowl, and you are not sure how you feel about any of it.

choices.label: Walk on to the bridge foot

scene_cult_pitch_say_no_kindly.narration: "No, thank you," you say, kindly. Hollis does not stop ladling. "That's alright, love," she says. "Soup's still free." She means it, which is the part that stays with you all the way to the bridge.

choices.label: Walk on to the bridge foot

scene_clerk.narration: At the bridge foot, a warden clerk named Pellam writes down every gem that crosses westbound, and keeps none of them. "Logged is not owned," he says. "Owned is not my department." A tagged caravan rolls up: gem 4117. As it passes, it hums, and his pen skips right off the page.

choices.label: Ask the carter what she'd take for it
Find a rule in Pellam's big book
Let it cross, and write down where it's going

check_carter.prompt: Talk a tired carter into trading gem 4117

onSuccess.narration: She has been listening to that gem hum for nine days. "Take it," she says. "Give me a song I can sing over it instead." You give her the best one you know.

onFailure.narration: "Promised to a buyer in the foothills," she says, and clicks to her mule. Gem 4117 hums away west across the bridge.

check_ledger.prompt: Find the rule that lets a logged gem change hands

onSuccess.narration: Page four hundred and twelve: a logged gem may be transferred at the crossing if both parties sign and the clerk is not on his lunch. Pellam checks his watch. He is not on his lunch.

onFailure.narration: You find a rule about goats, a rule about very large goats, and a rule about goats that are actually two children in a coat. By the time you look up, gem 4117 is across.

scene_clerk_stone.narration: Pellam crosses out WESTBOUND, writes EASTBOUND, crosses that out, and writes WITH THEM, pointing at you. "Very irregular," he says. "Entirely legal." The stone is cool and heavy, and its hum makes your teeth feel fizzy.

scene_engineers.narration: In the engineers' tent, a big chalk survey of the bridge is pinned up, every crack drawn in red. Engineer Brask, who has a pencil behind each ear and a third one she has forgotten about, says the cracks came with the tremors. Then she frowns at the drawing, as if it has just said something rude.

choices.label: Lay your evidence beside the survey
Tell her the cracks all lean one way
Unroll your copy of the old marks

check_outline.prompt: Plot everything you've seen since Bramblewood against the cracks

onSuccess.narration: You draw it in chalk yourselves: the troll's humming bridge, the bent pride roads, the spiralling sashes. Then you draw the cracks over the top.

onFailure.narration: Your map comes out looking like a cat walked across it. Brask takes the chalk, says "no, no, you're right, look," and draws it again properly.

scene_outline.narration: Everything points the same way. The troll's old note, the pride roads, the sashes, the cracks: all bending around the stones, and all of it older than the mountain's name. The stones did not come from the eruption. They were there first. And the land has been keeping records the whole time. Brask goes very quiet and sits down on a bucket.

rest_tent.narration: The engineers share their tea, which is very strong and has a tremor ripple in every cup. Outside, the bridge creaks like an old ship. Rest a while. You have the outline of the truth, and now you have to decide what to do with it.

scene_who_to_tell.narration: The wardens are right here: honest, careful, and already talking about acceptable losses. Out on the road, Nim the bell-rider is heading home to the gathering towns, who have kept the mountain's rules for a thousand years. Or you could fold the map up small and keep it. Who do you tell? Everybody vote.

choices.label: Send it north with Nim the bell-rider

scene_told_wardens.narration: Brask listens to all of it, writes all of it down, and underlines the bit about the mountain three times. "Thank you," she says, completely serious. "This changes the arithmetic." She tears a crossing pass out of her book. It is the first thing all day anybody has given away for free.

scene_told_gatherers.narration: You catch Nim just as Pepper is leaving. She listens to all of it, rings her bell once, high and clear, and says, "Grandmother is going to say she told everyone." Then she gallops north with your news, and Pepper, for once, does not argue.

scene_kept_close.narration: You fold the chalk map small, smaller, smallest, until it fits inside a boot. Nobody else knows. That is either very wise or very lonely, and you will find out which. Somewhere in your packs, the stones keep humming, as if they know too.

scene_crossing.narration: Your turn on the bridge. The cracked span sways a little under each cart, and a warden at the end waves you on, two at a time, with a flag. Below, the river is cold and loud. On the far side the land climbs toward a red sky.

choices.label: Take your ration turn on the span
Keep to the east rail, like the Brassbuckles' map says
Carry everyone over the gap, unofficially

check_span.prompt: Cross the swaying span before the warden's flag drops

onSuccess.narration: Step, sway, step, sway, and you're over. The warden at the far end gives you a very small nod, which from a Skywarden is practically a hug.

onFailure.narration: Halfway across, the bridge gives a long groan and the flag slams down. "Span closed! Everybody back!" The only other way over is the old pride ford, underneath.

scene_under_bridge.narration: Under the bridge the stone is warm from the sun, and somebody else has noticed. A pack of cinder wolves lies heaped against the pillars, ember-eyed and cold, a long way from home. They lift their heads at the hum in your packs and do not like it at all.

choices.label: Leave them your supper and tiptoe past

check_wolves.prompt: Get the pack interested in supper instead of you

onSuccess.narration: Every nose turns toward the supper. You wade the ford with your boots in your hands while a dozen ember eyes ignore you completely.

onFailure.narration: The supper is gone in four seconds. The pack looks at you as if to say: is that all?

encounter_wolves.narration: The pack spreads along both shallow crossings, guarding the warm side of the river.

onVictory.narration: The wolves give way, grumbling, and pile back up against their warm pillar. You wade across while they pretend they meant to move anyway.

onDefeat.narration: The pack holds the ford, and you end up back on the south bank, soggy and outnumbered.

scene_griffin_shortcut.narration: One at a time, you carry everybody over the broken gap, wings beating hard over the cold water. Behind you, clerk Pellam watches the whole thing, sighs, and writes UNRATIFIED in his ledger in very large letters.

scene_far_rim.narration: The far side climbs, and keeps climbing. The grass gets shorter, the stones get redder, and the sky ahead glows like the inside of a lantern. These are the foothills of Mount Red Sky, and you are coming down into them from the north-east, with the truth folded up in your packs.

rest_end.narration: You camp on the rim and look down. The foothills are full of tiny campfires, thousands of them, all the rush in the world. Above it all, the mountain glows. The stones hum. Somebody has to put this all together on one table, and tomorrow, at Redspire, the wardens' citadel, somebody will.

rest_setback.narration: Nobody is hurt. The wolves just wanted the warm side more. You wait two whole days on the south bank for the span to open again, while the rush gets further ahead and the mountain glows a little brighter every night. In the end Pellam waves you across himself. "Logged," he says. "Late. But logged."

scene_brass_south.narration: Coming south against the line is a wheelbarrow, pushed by six people in six very dented brass hats. The Brassbuckle Expedition. The wheelbarrow is empty. When they see you, they stop, and for once nobody is smiling smoothly. They just look tired.

choices.label: Ask them what happened up north

scene_brass_south_ask_what.narration: "Full," says the tallest Brassbuckle. "The foothills are full. Every stone has three people standing on it already, and a warden writing it down." He looks at the empty barrow. "We should have told the troll a story," he says. "We'd have been first, then. Probably." Nobody believes him, including him.

choices.label: Wish them a good road home

scene_brass_south_share_supper.narration: You share your supper with all six of them, sitting on the empty barrow. They eat like people who have not eaten since the foothills. Afterwards the smallest Brassbuckle gives you a folded paper. "Our map of the span," she says. "Keep to the east rail. It sways least. We were going to sell it."

scene_brass_south_ask_question.narration: "Where did you get that?" you ask, nodding at the barrow. "And where is it going?" The Brassbuckles look into it. There is nothing in it at all. "Nowhere, now," says the tallest at last. "Home." He sounds, for the first time since Stone Crossing, like he means it.

choices.label: Wish them a good road home

scene_tremor.narration: The ground shivers. Not a big shake: a long, low shudder, like a dog dreaming. The whole ration line wobbles. On the cart beside you a tall stack of crates begins to lean, and the tired carter driving it grabs for them too late.

choices.label: Look at what the shudder did to the road

check_crates.prompt: Catch a toppling stack of crates

onSuccess.narration: You catch the top crate, then the next, then the next, and stand there holding a wobbling tower until the carter props it back. "Nine days those have been humming at me," she says, wiping her face. "Nine days. Thank you." One crate has a tag on it: 4117.

onFailure.narration: The crates topple straight past your hands and land, thump, thump, thump, in a hay cart. Nothing breaks. One of them bursts open, and it is full of socks. "Not that one," says the tired carter. "The humming ones are underneath." One tag says 4117.

scene_tremor_look_down.narration: When the shudder stops, the road at your feet is crazed with cracks as thin as hairs. Dozens of them. And every one leans the same way, like grass in a wind, and the wind is coming from the mountain. You look up at the cracked bridge. Its cracks lean the same way too.

scene_nim_pony.narration: A very small, very fast pony has stopped dead in the road and will not take one more step toward the gem carts. On its back a dragonling about your size is ringing a bell at it, crossly. "Come ON, Pepper." She is Nim, a bell-rider for the gathering towns up north, and she is very late.

choices.label: Cover Pepper's ears and lead her past
Talk to Pepper, slow and quiet

scene_nim_pony_hold_pony.narration: You put your hands gently over Pepper's ears and lead her past the humming carts, one slow step at a time. Pepper allows this, as long as you also scratch her nose. "Grandmother says the ponies always know first," Nim tells you. "Grandmother says a lot of things. She is usually right. It's very annoying."

choices.label: Walk on with Nim to the bridge foot

check_pony.prompt: Talk a frightened pony past the humming carts

onSuccess.narration: You talk to Pepper about nothing: grass, apples, the weather. Her ears come forward. She sighs, and walks on past the carts as if it had been her idea all along. Nim stares at you. "Grandmother can do that," she says. "Nobody else can do that."

onFailure.narration: You talk to Pepper. Pepper talks back, loudly, and sits down in the road like a dog. In the end Nim gets off and you all push from behind, and Pepper walks on past the carts with her nose in the air, pretending she was always going to.

scene_nim_pony_bell_greeting.narration: You bow and ring an imaginary bell three times, high, low, high, the way they do in the gathering towns. Nim squeaks. "You're from the towns!" Even Pepper looks impressed. Nim walks with you all the way to the bridge foot, telling you which grandmothers are feuding this year. It is most of them.

choices.label: Walk on with Nim to the bridge foot

scene_old_marks.narration: Down at the bridge foot, where the river has scrubbed the oldest stones bare, there are marks. Carved lines, worn almost smooth, under the bridge's own stones, as if the bridge had been built on top of somebody else's writing. "Always been there," says a passing warden. "Nobody reads them."

choices.label: Make a charcoal rubbing of the marks
Lay a palm on the stone, like Old Lintel
Look at the marks the way your people read paths

check_rubbing.prompt: Rub charcoal over marks worn almost smooth

onSuccess.narration: Paper, charcoal, rub, rub, rub. The lines come up black and clear: a spiral, curling round and round a little circle in the middle. Just like the sashes at the waystation. Just like the pride roads. You roll the paper up very carefully.

onFailure.narration: Paper, charcoal, rub. What comes out is a perfect picture of a warden's boot, because a warden was standing on the corner of your paper. She asks if she can keep it. You let her.

scene_old_marks_palm.narration: You lay a palm flat on the old stone, the way Old Lintel does. For a long moment, nothing. Then, deep down, so low you feel it more than hear it: the note. The same note your packs hum. The stone under the bridge was humming it long before there was any bridge, or any rush.

choices.label: Go up to the clerk's table

scene_old_marks_read_marks.narration: You notice what everybody walks past. These marks are not just old. They have been carved again, and again, over hundreds of years, the old cuts deepened, the spiral kept clear. Somebody, or something, has been keeping this record for a very long time. You copy every line.

choices.label: Go up to the clerk's table

scene_survey_guard.narration: Outside the engineers' tent stands Corporal Tibbet, who is very new, very junior, and very serious. His helmet is too big. "No entry," he says, "without a pass. Or a reason. A good reason. In writing." He holds out a clipboard. It already has a pencil on a string.

choices.label: Tell him why you need to see the survey
Write your reason down, as asked
Show him the stone Pellam logged to you

check_tibbet.prompt: Convince a very serious corporal to let you in

onSuccess.narration: You tell him about the troll's note, and the bent roads, and the spiralling sashes. Tibbet listens with his mouth slightly open. Then he remembers he is a corporal, closes it, salutes, and lifts the tent flap for you.

onFailure.narration: Tibbet listens to every word, writes "REASON: LONG" on his clipboard, and says no. Then an engineer pokes her head out, says "Tibbet, let them hold the string," and pulls you round the side of the tent.

scene_survey_guard_write_it.narration: You write your reason on his clipboard, in your best letters: WE THINK THE STONES ARE OLDER THAN THE MOUNTAIN. Tibbet reads it. He reads it again. He goes slightly pale under the big helmet, and holds the tent flap open for you without another word.

scene_survey_guard_clerks_stone.narration: You show Tibbet the Clerk's Stone, tag 4117, with WITH THEM written in Pellam's hand. Tibbet reads the tag, stands up very straight, and salutes the stone. Then, because he is not sure, he salutes you too. "Logged goods may pass," he says, and opens the flap.

scene_crack_string.narration: Behind the tent, two apprentice engineers are kneeling at the end of the bridge, measuring the biggest crack with a knotted string. Every evening, at the same time, they measure it and chalk the date beside it. There is a long ladder of chalk marks now. "Hold this end?" one of them asks.

choices.label: Read the ladder of chalk marks

check_string.prompt: Hold a measuring string steady over a crack

onSuccess.narration: You hold it steady as a heron's leg. The apprentice counts the knots, then counts again. "A hair wider than yesterday," she says, and chalks it. "It's always a hair wider than yesterday." She says it as if she is getting tired of hair.

onFailure.narration: A breeze catches the string and it wiggles like a worm. You try again. It wiggles more. The apprentice laughs, measures it herself in a moment, and chalks the mark. "A hair wider than yesterday," she says. "Always is."

scene_crack_string_read_chalk.narration: Chalk marks climb the crack, one for every evening since the eruption, each a hair further along. Most days the step is tiny. Some days it jumps. Next to the jumps, somebody has written the number of gem carts that crossed that day. Nobody has written what that means.

scene_engineers_rubbing.narration: You unroll the copy of the old marks from under the bridge and lay it beside the survey. Brask looks from one to the other, and back again. The spiral on the old stone and the cracks in her new drawing curl round the very same point. She takes the pencil from behind her left ear, and then the right.

choices.label: Let her see the whole thing

choice_stones_on_table.narration: Brask looks up from her bucket at your packs. "Those are humming," she says. "Everything you've carried. May I see them? On the survey?" The whole tent goes quiet to hear what you'll say. Will you lay your stones on the table? Everybody vote.

choices.label: Lay every stone on the survey
Show her the Pride Stone that no pride would touch

choice_stones_on_table_lay_out.narration: You set your stones out on the big chalk drawing, one by one. They hum together, a little chord. Brask's tea starts to ripple in its cup. Without seeming to notice, she moves the cup to the far end of the table, then a bit further, then puts it on the floor.

choice_stones_on_table_keep_shut.narration: "Not yet," you say, and keep your packs shut. Brask nods slowly. "Fair," she says. "You carried them." She writes KEPT SHUT in the corner of the survey, very neatly, and underlines it, which makes you feel both proud and a little bit watched.

choice_stones_on_table_pride_stone.narration: You set the Pride Stone on the table and tell her where it came from: the middle of the widest bend, where no pride would set a paw. Brask writes PRIDE COUNTRY: AVOIDED BY EVERYONE on her survey and draws a circle round it. Then she draws a second circle round that one.

scene_span_question.narration: At the bridge end, the warden with the flag stops you. She looks at your packs, and then at you, and asks, very seriously, "Where did you get that? And where is it going?" It is Old Lintel's question, word for word, a whole country away from his bridge.

choices.label: Ask where she heard that question
Tell her the river asked you first

scene_span_question_answer.narration: You tell her all of it, from the Exchange gutter to the bridge foot, as honestly as you can. She writes it down. At the end she looks at what she has written for quite a while. "Nobody else has answered properly," she says. "They just say 'mine' and 'north.'"

scene_span_question_ask_back.narration: "From a carter," she says, "who had it from a centaur, who had it from a manticore, who had it from a troll, apparently." She shrugs. "It's a good question. Everybody's asking it now. Nobody has a good answer." She waves her flag at the next cart and asks them too.

scene_span_question_river_asked.narration: "The river asked us first," you say. "It took us all the way to the sea to ask it." The warden blinks. Then she laughs, a real laugh, the first one you have heard from a Skywarden. "Well," she says, "did you have an answer for it?" You are still working on that.

scene_pack_crossing.narration: Pellam comes down the line with his big book. "Humming goods," he announces, "may cross on the wardens' gem cart, logged. Or in your own arms, also logged. The span shivers either way." He licks his pencil. "Logged is not owned. Your choice."

choices.label: Send them over on the gem cart
Wrap them in Ossley's reed knot first

scene_pack_crossing_carry.narration: "We'll carry them," you say. Pellam writes CARRIED, BY HAND, BY CHOICE in his book. You hug your packs tight. They feel heavier than they did this morning, though nothing has been put in them. Pellam looks at them over his spectacles and says nothing, which for Pellam is a lot.

scene_pack_crossing_cart.narration: You load your packs on the gem cart with all the others. It hums like a hive. As it rolls onto the span, the whole bridge gives a long, low groan, and every warden on it stops and looks down at their boots. Then the cart is over, and the bridge is just a bridge again.

scene_pack_crossing_reed_knot.narration: You wind Old Ossley's wet reed knot round your packs, and the hum goes soft, like a river a long way off. Pellam leans close and listens. He writes HUMMING GOODS, and crosses it out, and writes QUIETER THAN EXPECTED. "Most irregular," he says, and sounds pleased.

check_span_quiet.prompt: Cross along the steady east rail before the flag drops

onSuccess.narration: Along the east rail the span hardly sways at all. You walk over almost easily, and the warden at the far end gives you a very small nod. The Brassbuckles' map was right. You hope somebody tells them.

onFailure.narration: The east rail is steadier, but not steady enough. Halfway over, the bridge groans and the flag slams down. "Span closed! Everybody back!" The only other way over is the old pride ford, underneath.

scene_rim_lookout.narration: On the rim stands a centaur road marker, freshly painted: REDSPIRE, ONE DAY. Below, the foothills glitter with campfires. Then hooves drum up the road behind you, and Bracken Swiftmile skids to a stop, sash stuffed with letters. "Relay waits for nobody," she pants. "But it does catch up. Anything going south?"

choices.label: Send word south to the pride and the troll
Fly up and look for Redspire

scene_rim_lookout_send_word.narration: You write two short letters. One for Elder Sefa: the cubs were right, the stones really are singing. One for Old Lintel: we are finding out. Bracken tucks them in her sash. "Troll'll take a year to read it," she says. "He'll hear every word, though." Then she is gone, south, at a gallop.

check_fires.prompt: Count the rush's campfires in the foothills below

onSuccess.narration: You count in hundreds, then in patches, then in valleys. Bracken helps. Your best guess is four thousand and twelve, and Bracken writes it down to carry south. "Biggest rush in living memory," she says, and whistles. "And all of it humming."

onFailure.narration: One, two, three... you lose count at three hundred and something, when a cloud moves and a whole valley of fires appears at once. "More than stars," says Bracken, and that will have to do. She trots off south with your news.

scene_rim_lookout_fly_redspire.narration: You climb high into the red evening. Far off, on the highest peak of the foothills, stands a tall black citadel, shining like a wet stone: Redspire, where the wardens keep their records. Every road in the foothills seems to lead to it. You glide back down and tell Bracken. She already knew, but she lets you tell her anyway.

llmHints.tone: busy, gray-coated, a bit solemn, with warm people in it; the moment the party sees the whole shape of the clue
forbidden: the cult as villains; they are kind first, always
naming what the titan or the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.hollis: a Deep Hollow Cult recruiter with a giant soup pot; gentle, patient, calls everyone 'love'; feeds people before she says anything; sincerely believes the seal is a lid on a cure
npcVoices.pellam: a Skywarden clerk; dry, precise, logs everything and keeps nothing; 'logged is not owned'; secretly enjoys irregular-but-legal
npcVoices.brask: Skywarden engineer; pencils behind both ears; blunt and honest; talks about arithmetic and acceptable losses but is not unkind
npcVoices.carter: a tired caravan driver; has heard gem 4117 hum for nine days; trades for a song; grateful when you catch her crates
npcVoices.nim: a dragonling bell-rider on a tiny fast pony called Pepper; quick, proud, a little cheeky about her grandmother
npcVoices.brassbuckles: the Brassbuckle Expedition, coming home south with an empty wheelbarrow and dented hats; tired, honest for once
npcVoices.tibbet: Corporal Tibbet, a very new Skywarden guarding the engineers' tent; helmet too big; wants reasons in writing
npcVoices.apprentice: an apprentice engineer measuring the crack with knotted string every evening; 'a hair wider than yesterday'
npcVoices.flag_warden: the Skywarden with the flag at the span; asks the troll's question of every cart
npcVoices.bracken_swiftmile: a relay-running centaur stuffed with letters; quick, cheerful; 'relay waits for nobody, but it does catch up'
